correctness.rationale: All square and pairwise anti equations follow by literal multiplication, without division by two. A nonzero middle superdiagonal vector forces its neighbors to vanish. The b=0 branch is exactly a linear space of singular 2x2 auxiliary matrices; its rank-one subspaces have the common-image/common-kernel dichotomy over any field. Proper incidence bundles and generic uniqueness give two rational components of dimension 3r+1, while a linear branch has dimension 4r. Distinct rank-two witnesses and b≠0 examples show exactly three maximal components. Determinantal rank stratification gives all three pairwise intersection dimensions; finite-field counting by rank 0,1,2 plus inclusion-exclusion proves the formula over all q. Twelve complete finite-field checks over q=2,3,4,5 at r=1,2,3 matched. Computations only corroborate the proof.

value.rationale: The moduli of exterior-algebra generators acting strictly along a fixed four-step flag are a natural constrained representation problem. This single theorem completely classifies their reduced irreducible components and intersection geometry for every r>=2, with a uniform formula for exact rational points over every finite field and even-characteristic behavior. The rank-one Segre ruling turns a nonlinear multi-relation problem into two canonical families; the result is not a selected small numerical computation or a trivial consequence of generic unrestricted commuting varieties.
